title: 2013 AMC 12B Problem 14
statement: Two non-decreasing sequences of nonnegative integers have different first terms. Each sequence has the property that each term beginning with the third is the sum of the previous two terms, and the seventh term of each sequence is \(N.\) What is the smallest possible value of \(N?\)

solutions.text: A sequence starting \(a_1, a_2\) has seventh term \(5a_1 + 8a_2.\) For the two sequences, \(5a_1 + 8a_2 = 5b_1 + 8b_2,\) so \(5(b_1 - a_1) = 8(a_2 - b_2).\) Since \(\gcd(5, 8) = 1,\) we need \(b_1 - a_1\) to be a multiple of \(8\) and \(a_2 - b_2\) to be a multiple of \(5.\) Taking \(a_1 \lt b_1\) with nondecreasing terms gives \(a_1 \le b_1 - 8 \le b_2 - 8 \le a_2 - 13.\) Choosing \(a_1 = 0,\) \(b_1 = b_2 = 8,\) \(a_2 = 13\) yields \(N = 5\cdot 0 + 8\cdot 13 = 104.\) Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: In terms of the first two terms \(a_1, a_2,\) the seventh term equals \(5a_1 + 8a_2\)
Setting the two seventh terms equal gives \(5(b_1 - a_1) = 8(a_2 - b_2);\) coprimality of \(5\) and \(8\) forces \(b_1 - a_1\) to be a multiple of \(8\)
